column1: # The one table both copies of "remove only strictly under a root" answer (docs/known-copies.toml, safe-remove-under): the Rust
# canonical (tools/paddock-dev/src/safe_remove/guard.rs, `remove_under`) and the shell copy (conformance/ci/safe-rm.sh, `safe_rm`).
# Read by guard.rs's tests and by conformance/test/safe-rm.test.mjs; a row changes for both or for neither.
# The tree, made fresh for every row under a scratch folder <B>:
#   <B>/root/a/b/f              a folder with a file
#   <B>/outside/keep/f          what must never go
#   <B>/root/link -> <B>/outside   a link to a folder outside the root
#   <B>/rootlink -> <B>/root       a link to the root
# Columns (tab separated): name, root, target, result, gone.
#   result: ok (exit 0 / Ok) or refused (exit 1 / Err(Refused)).
#   gone: the path below <B> that is gone afterwards, or - when nothing is removed. Every row also checks that
#   <B>/outside/keep/f is still there and, for a refused row, that <B>/root/a/b/f is too.
#   A result `ok-fold|refused-nofold` is ok where names are compared without case (macOS, Windows) and refused elsewhere.
# On Windows, guard.rs's `the_shared_parity_table_holds_in_windows_spelling` runs the rows without a link in Windows spelling
# (`\` separators, and each target again as `\\?\<path>`). Not covered there: the link rows (a symlink needs Developer Mode or
# an elevated token) and the shell copy (Windows CI does not run conformance/test/safe-rm.test.mjs).
name
a folder strictly under the root
a file strictly under the root
a path that is not there
a final link goes as a link
a final link with a trailing slash goes as a link, never what it names
a final link with a trailing slash and dot goes as a link
a final link with two trailing slashes goes as a link
a link in the middle is refused
a .. that climbs out is refused
a .. that stays inside is refused too
the root itself is refused
the root with a trailing slash is the root
a path outside the root is refused
a root with a trailing slash works
known limit: a root that is a link is read as written, not resolved
names differ in case
